LRU-based origin tracking and pruning record logic for gossip duplicates.

# Purpose
`fd_prune_finder.c` implements the state management for a prune-finder component that tracks origins by public key and keeps them in both a hash map and an LRU list. It defines the internal `fd_prune_origin_t` record, which stores the origin identity, an upsert counter, and link fields for the pool, map chain, and LRU list. The file also instantiates generic pool, doubly linked list, and chained map templates for `fd_prune_origin_t`, `origin_map`, and `lru_list`, so the code can allocate, look up, remove, and reorder origin records with fixed-size storage.

The main entry point is [`fd_prune_finder_record`](<#fd_prune_finder_record>), which records activity for an `origin_pubkey` and updates the LRU order. If the origin is not already present, the function acquires a record from the free pool or reuses the oldest LRU entry, clears and stores the new key, inserts the record into the map, and appends it to the LRU tail. If the origin already exists, the function moves it to the LRU tail to mark it as recently used. The function also increments `num_upserts` when `num_dups` is zero, which lets the prune-finder track unique upsert events for each origin.
